items.front: The lateral rectus is supplied by which cranial nerve? [___]
items.context: The lateral rectus is the horizontal muscle that moves the eye away from the nose. Its motor supply is from cranial nerve VI.

items.front: Which movement is produced primarily by the medial rectus? [___]
items.context: The medial rectus is the horizontal muscle that moves the eye towards the nose. It is supplied by the inferior division of cranial nerve III.

items.front: A lesion of the abducens nucleus causes an ipsilateral horizontal [___] palsy.
items.context:
The abducens nucleus contains motor neurons for the ipsilateral lateral rectus.

Interneurons cross before ascending in the contralateral medial longitudinal fasciculus to the opposite medial rectus subnucleus, so the nucleus coordinates horizontal gaze.

items.front: Which ocular motor nerve is vulnerable to stretch in raised intracranial pressure because of its long, tethered intracranial course? [___]
items.context:
After leaving the pons, the sixth nerve ascends along the clivus and passes over the petrous apex beneath the petrosphenoidal ligament in Dorello's canal.

Its long, tethered course makes it vulnerable to stretch when intracranial pressure rises.

items.front: In the cavernous sinus, the abducens nerve lies immediately beside the internal [___] artery.
items.context:
Within the cavernous sinus, the sixth nerve runs beside the internal carotid artery rather than in the lateral dural wall.

A cavernous-sinus process can therefore produce sixth-nerve palsy with other ocular motor or trigeminal findings.
